say.text: A 58-year-old man has a distended abdomen. The supine film shows dilated central loops with regular folds in a 'stack of coins' pattern.
Which bowel is dilated, and which marker shows it?
Yes. Valvulae conniventes cross the full width of the lumen, and they mark the small bowel.
The loops sit centrally, which is the small bowel picture, not the large bowel's peripheral one.
Tempting: haustra are the large bowel's marker, and you have spotted folds on the film.
Check the position first. Where do these loops lie, centrally or at the edge of the abdomen?
Haustra do mark the large bowel, but they stop short of the lumen, and these loops lie centrally.
Here the folds cross the full width, which is the valvulae conniventes of small bowel.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so re-check the rule: valvulae cross the full width and mark small bowel; haustra stop short and mark large bowel.

say.text: Tempting: haustra are the folds most often pictured on a film, so the familiar marker feels right.
Look at the folds again. Do they cross the full width of the lumen, or stop short of it?
Haustra are real, but they stop short of the lumen and belong to the large bowel.
The folds here cross the full width, so the marker is valvulae conniventes, and the bowel is small.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so pin the pair: valvulae cross the full width and mark the small bowel; haustra stop short.

say.text: On a plain film of a distended abdomen, the radiologist measures the loops against the 3-6-9 rule.
What is the upper normal diameter of the small bowel?
Yes. Small bowel's upper normal diameter is 3 cm, widening to 6 cm in the colon and 9 cm in the caecum.
Calibre rises from small bowel to caecum, so a small bowel loop above 3 cm is dilated.
Tempting: 6 cm is the colon's limit, and it is the middle number you have just heard.
Think about calibre. Which segment is the narrowest, and which number belongs to it?
6 cm is the colon's upper normal, not the small bowel's.
Small bowel is the narrowest segment, so its limit is the smallest number: 3 cm.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so re-learn the ladder: 3 small, 6 colon, 9 caecum, each widening towards the caecum.

say.text: Tempting: 9 cm is the largest number on the rule, so it feels like the 'big bowel' answer.
Ask which segment is narrowest. Its limit is the smallest number, so check that one.
9 cm is the caecum's upper normal, the widest segment, not the small bowel's.
The small bowel's upper normal is 3 cm.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so anchor the rule to calibre: the numbers rise as the bowel widens, small bowel lowest, caecum highest.

say.text: Another supine film of a distended abdomen. The question is about a dilated small bowel loop.
Which feature is NOT seen in that loop?
Right. Haustra belong to the large bowel, and they stop short of the lumen. Small bowel loops lie centrally.
So the peripheral loop with haustra is the feature a dilated small bowel loop does not show.
Tempting: a dilated bowel is often picked out by its central position, so central loops look like a feature to rule out.
But central loops are the small bowel picture, so they are seen here, not excluded.
The feature the question wants is the peripheral loop with haustra, the large bowel pattern.
Tempting: folds are what you look for on a film, and these are the ones that cross the lumen.
But valvulae conniventes cross the full width and mark the small bowel, so they are seen here, not excluded.
The NOT feature is the peripheral loop with haustra, which belongs to the large bowel.
A plain film report in an adult with distension gives small bowel 4 cm, transverse colon 5 cm and caecum 7 cm.
Which segment is dilated?

choices.label: The small bowel and the caecum
The caecum, as the widest segment

say.text: Yes. Small bowel at 4 cm is above its 3 cm limit; the colon at 5 cm and caecum at 7 cm are under 6 cm and 9 cm.
Apply each segment's own limit, and only the small bowel is dilated.
Tempting: 7 cm looks large when you have the colon's 6 cm in mind.
Each segment has its own limit. Which limit applies to the caecum, and is 7 cm above it?
The caecum's upper normal is 9 cm, so 7 cm is normal; you borrowed the colon's 6 cm.
The small bowel is the only segment above its own limit: 4 cm against 3 cm.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so apply each segment's own limit, not the nearest number you remember.

say.text: Tempting: the caecum has the biggest number, so it feels like the dilated one. Raw size is not the test.
Check each segment against its own limit, one at a time. Which of them is above its limit?
The colon at 5 cm is under its 6 cm limit, and the caecum at 7 cm is under its 9 cm limit.
Only the small bowel, at 4 cm against 3 cm, is dilated.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so remember that the limits differ by segment: 3 small, 6 colon, 9 caecum.

say.text: An adult has vomiting, distension and no flatus, and obstruction is suspected.
Which investigation is the investigation of choice to confirm small bowel obstruction and show its cause?
Yes. Contrast-enhanced CT is the investigation of choice for small bowel obstruction: it shows the level, the cause and the signs of strangulation.
A plain film is the initial test; it shows that obstruction is present, not why.
Tempting: the erect and supine X-ray is the first test you order, and it does show dilated bowel.
Ask what each test answers. Which one shows the level and cause, not just that the bowel is blocked?
A plain X-ray is the initial test for suspected obstruction; it shows that the bowel is blocked, not its cause or strangulation.
The definitive test for small bowel obstruction is contrast-enhanced CT, which shows the transition point and the cause.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so keep two tests apart: X-ray is the first test, CT the definitive one for small bowel obstruction.

say.text: Tempting: ultrasound is quick and at the bedside, and it is the test you use for a child with intussusception.
Ask which disease that test is for. Is it the investigation of choice for an adult with small bowel obstruction?
Ultrasound is the investigation of choice for intussusception in children, not for small bowel obstruction in adults.
For adult small bowel obstruction, contrast-enhanced CT is the investigation of choice.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so attach each test to its disease: ultrasound for a child's intussusception, CT for adult small bowel obstruction.

say.text: A ladder for three questions: the first test for suspected obstruction, the definitive test for small bowel obstruction, and the test of choice for a child with suspected intussusception.
Which ladder is correct, in that order?

choices.label: Plain film; contrast CT; contrast enema

say.text: Right. Plain film first, contrast CT for the definitive answer in small bowel obstruction, and ultrasound for a child with intussusception.
Tempting: CT is the most definitive test you know, so it feels like the first step too.
But you start with a plain film, and CT comes after obstruction is confirmed, as the definitive test.
Right ladder: plain film, then contrast CT, then ultrasound for a child with intussusception.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so order the tests: the test that starts the work-up is not the one that settles the diagnosis.

say.text: Tempting: the contrast enema is the test you link with intussusception, so it feels right for a child.
But in a child the investigation of choice is ultrasound, which shows the target or doughnut sign.
So the ladder for a child starts with ultrasound, and the enema is not the first test.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so keep the child's test apart: ultrasound first, with its target or doughnut sign.

say.text: Plain film: a massively dilated loop arises from the pelvis and is shaped like a coffee bean.
Which diagnosis fits this sign?
Yes. The coffee bean, or bent inner tube, is the plain film sign of sigmoid volvulus.
On contrast enema the same twist shows as a bird's beak, and on CT as a whirl sign.
Tempting: both are volvulus, and both show as a dilated loop on the same plain film.
Check the site. The stem places the loop in the pelvis; where does a caecal volvulus sit?
Caecal volvulus is a dilated, kidney-shaped caecum displaced to the left upper quadrant, not a coffee-bean loop from the pelvis.
The coffee bean, bent inner tube or omega sign is the plain film sign of sigmoid volvulus.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so link the shape to the site: a coffee bean from the pelvis is sigmoid; a kidney-shaped caecum in the left upper quadrant is caecal.

say.text: Tempting: a coiled bowel loop can look like a target or a claw, so you may have pinned this shape on intussusception.
Name the shape first, then the disease it belongs to. Which disease carries the coffee-bean sign?
Intussusception shows the target or doughnut on ultrasound and the claw on contrast enema, not a coffee bean.
The coffee bean is the plain film sign of sigmoid volvulus.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so keep each sign with its disease and modality: the coffee bean is sigmoid volvulus on plain film.

say.text: Each sign below belongs to one disease and one imaging test.
Which pairing of sign and test is correct?

choices.label: Claw on plain film; target on ultrasound
Claw on enema; target on ultrasound
Bird's beak on plain film; target on ultrasound

say.text: Right. The claw sign sits at the apex of the intussusceptum on contrast enema; the target sign is on ultrasound.
Tempting: the claw sounds like a bowel-gas sign, so a plain film feels like enough to find it.
But the claw sign is seen at the apex of the intussusceptum on contrast enema, not on a plain film.
Right pairing: claw on contrast enema, target on ultrasound.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so pin the claw to the enema: a plain film does not show it.

say.text: Tempting: the bird's beak is a sigmoid volvulus shape, so it feels as if it belongs with the plain film coffee bean.
But the bird's beak is the tapering twist seen on contrast enema, not on a plain film.
Right pairing: claw on contrast enema, target on ultrasound.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so keep the bird's beak with the enema, and the coffee bean with the plain film.

say.text: To finish: a plain film is the first test for obstruction, contrast CT is definitive for small bowel obstruction, and ultrasound is the test for a child's intussusception.
Coffee bean is sigmoid volvulus, bird's beak and claw are on enema, and target and pseudokidney are on ultrasound.
